prompt: Two equivalents of a thiol (2 RSH) are treated with mild oxidant (I₂ or Br₂, base). What's the product?

options.label: A disulfide (R-S-S-R) — two S's covalently linked, oxidant is reduced to X⁻
A sulfoxide (R-S(=O)-R) — one S has become doubly bonded to oxygen
A sulfone (R-SO₂-R) — one S has been oxidized all the way to the S(VI) oxidation state
Just the deprotonated thiolate R-S⁻ with X⁻ counterion — oxidation requires harsher conditions

explanation: Thiols oxidize easily to disulfides (2 R-SH + I₂ → R-S-S-R + 2 HI). This is the Cys → cystine chemistry in proteins (crucial for stabilizing tertiary structure, e.g., insulin). Reduction (Zn/HCl, DTT, TCEP) reverses it. Sulfoxide and sulfone require harsher oxidants (mCPBA, H₂O₂).
